name: Hōkūleʻa built
summary: Hōkūleʻa, a double-hulled Polynesian voyaging canoe rebuilt with modern plywood and fibreglass, was launched in 1975 to test ancient long-distance voyaging by actually sailing.
description: Double-hulled voyaging canoe with cold-molded plywood hulls covered in fiberglass, built for experimental voyaging.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.
why: Scholars disputed whether ancient Polynesians could have sailed deliberately between distant islands, and a sailing replica offered a practical test.

market.note: This is the particular custom vessel built by a nonprofit voyaging society for experimental and cultural voyages, as described by a founder. That mission supports a practical-use anchor for this vessel; funding, paid work or later commerce are not ruled out.

events.statement: The PVS canoe departed on its Hawaiʻi–Tahiti research voyage, guided by Mau Piailug using non-instrument wayfinding.
events.caveats: Practice voyages occurred before 1976 and modifications followed 1975 swamping; this anchor identifies the intended project voyage and does not claim first use of any kind. earliest_record.rationale: Earliest defensible dated record of this scoped referent in the retained evidence; later community entry is recorded separately. The documented 8 March launch establishes that the vessel had been built by then; the inspected sources do not establish a specific construction-completion date. The completion date of construction is not specified; launch does not by itself establish practical research deployment. This is the earliest supported record currently established here, not certification of absolute priority.

community_entry.rationale: Documented crew training on the completed canoe in April 1975 is an earlier actual crew use than the later 1976 Tahiti project voyage.
community_entry.caveats: The photograph captions give April but not an exact day or first training sail. The 1976 interview is retrospective and does not itself date a particular practice; the distinct 1 May 1976 research voyage and 1975 swamping remain separate.

caveats: Modern reconstruction; successful voyages cannot by themselves authenticate every ancient design or migration route. Practice under sail preceded the 1976 research voyage; the anchor is the documented intended project voyage, not a claim that no earlier use occurred.

links.statement: The team used a comparison-based hypothesis about earlier canoe forms to select Hōkūleʻa’s design.
links.alternatives: Different reconstruction choices and modern hull designs were available.
links.caveats: Modern materials and uncertain historical reconstruction remain explicit.
links.timing: 1973 design work precedes the documented 1975 launch.
